content:
Perimeter and area make their Class 4 debut — and Olympiad papers immediately mix them with cost and fencing twists. Here is what the IMO Class 4 perimeter and area chapter tests, the formulas, the classic mix-up, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 4 Maths Olympiad Perimeter and Area chapter tests

  • Perimeter of squares, rectangles and irregular shapes
  • Area of squares and rectangles; counting squares on a grid
  • Choosing the right units (cm vs sq cm)
  • Fencing, tiling and cost word problems

Key facts your child should know

  • P(rectangle) = 2 × (l + b); P(square) = 4 × side.
  • A(rectangle) = l × b; A(square) = side × side.
  • Perimeter is a length (cm, m); area is in square units (sq cm, sq m).
  • Fencing/border → perimeter; tiling/carpet → area; cost = amount × rate.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Using area when the problem is about a border or fence.
  • Adding only two sides for a rectangle’s perimeter.
  • Writing area in cm instead of sq cm.

quiz.title: IMO Class 4 Perimeter and Area Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: IMO Maths Olympiad Class 4: Perimeter and Area

questions.q: The perimeter of a rectangular drawing sheet is 72 cm and its breadth is 15 cm. What is its length?
questions.explanation: Length + breadth = perimeter ÷ 2 = 72 ÷ 2 = 36 cm. So length = 36 − 15 = 21 cm.

questions.q: A square scarf has each side 11 dm. A bigger square scarf has sides twice as long. What is the area of the bigger scarf?
questions.explanation: The bigger side = 2 × 11 = 22 dm. Area = 22 × 22 = 484 sq dm (four times the small area of 121 sq dm).

questions.q: The length of a rectangular garden is 12 m and its breadth is 8 m. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (length + breadth) = 2 × (12 + 8) = 2 × 20 = 40 m.

questions.q: A kitchen wall measuring 16 m by 8 m is to be covered fully with square tiles of side 4 m. How many tiles are needed?
questions.explanation: Floor area = 16 × 8 = 128 sq m. One tile covers 4 × 4 = 16 sq m. Tiles needed = 128 ÷ 16 = 8.

questions.q: On a 1-cm squared grid, a star shape covers 12 full squares and 8 half squares. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Each full square = 1 sq cm and 2 half squares make 1 sq cm. Area = 12 + 8 ÷ 2 = 12 + 4 = 16 sq cm.

questions.q: Two rectangular mats, one 12 m by 4 m and another 10 m by 6 m, have equal perimeters. How much larger is the area of the second mat?
questions.explanation: Both perimeters equal 32 m. Areas: 12 × 4 = 48 sq m and 10 × 6 = 60 sq m. Difference = 60 − 48 = 12 sq m.

questions.q: The area of a rectangular carpet is 96 sq m. If its length is 12 m, what is its breadth?
It costs Rs 200 per square metre to polish a rectangular stage floor that is 9 m by 7 m. Find the total cost.
The perimeter of a rectangular vegetable patch is 40 m and its length is 12 m. Find its breadth.
questions.explanation: Length + breadth = perimeter ÷ 2 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 m. So breadth = 20 − 12 = 8 m.

questions.q: A rectangular rose garden is 20 m long and 15 m wide. Fencing costs Rs 8 per metre. What is the total cost of fencing it once around?
questions.explanation: Fence length = perimeter = 2 × (20 + 15) = 70 m. Cost = 70 × 8 = Rs 560.

faq.q: When do I use perimeter and when area?
faq.a: Perimeter for anything going around (fence, border, frame, lace); area for anything covering the surface (tiles, carpet, paint).

faq.q: What is the area of a 16 dm × 13 dm sheet?
faq.a: 16 × 13 = 208 sq dm — multiply length by breadth.
